title: Where the milliseconds go
sub: Time to first byte for a fresh HTTPS connection from Mumbai.

frames.caption: A user in Mumbai opens a new HTTPS connection straight to an origin in Virginia, about 150 ms away round trip. TCP needs one round trip, TLS 1.3 another, and the request a third: 460 ms before the first byte arrives, almost all of it the speed of light in fiber.
The same request to a CDN edge in Mumbai, 20 ms away, with the file in its cache. The same three round trips now cost 62 ms in total: 7 times faster, and the origin never sees the request.

A cache miss at the edge. The handshakes are still local and fast; only the edge's fetch crosses the ocean, over a connection it keeps open to the origin, so it costs one long round trip instead of three. 220 ms: better than going direct, and every later request for that file is a hit.
